answer: Cross-chain identity binding at the nectar pool: one KYC-anchored identity can mint across chains but all instances share a single staking pool. The ridge check reconciles balances across bridges, flagging any address whose linked identities exceed the cap. A sybil farm spanning five chains gets caught at the lantern, where merged stake collapses to one unit — five times the gas, one-fifth the yield. Works because cross-chain proof makes duplication costlier than honesty.
